bugs.title: use_decoupled_grad set wrong for bf16 + use_precision_aware_optimizer
bugs.root_cause: The condition for enabling FusedAdam master_weights was 'if config.main_params_dtype != torch.float32 or config.fp8_recipe == "delayed"'. This was True for bf16 main params even when the higher-level path (e.g. TE-managed master weights) should have owned them, double-managing master copies and silently using wrong precision in the optimizer step.
bugs.invariant: FusedAdam master_weights flag must equal config.use_precision_aware_optimizer_no_fp8_or_ds_fp8.

bugs.title: group_limited_topk used hardcoded k=2 instead of num_groups/group_topk
bugs.root_cause: group_limited_topk computed group_scores as scores.view(num_tokens, num_groups, -1).topk(2, dim=-1)[0].sum(dim=-1) — the k=2 was hardcoded instead of using num_groups//group_topk. This produced wrong group scores and therefore wrong group selection for token-to-expert routing in DeepSeek-style models.
bugs.invariant: group_scores must equal sum of top-(num_groups//group_topk) routing scores within each group (correctness check on the topk k value).

bugs.title: MoE topk=1 gradient is silently zero because softmax is applied post-topk on a [N,1] tensor
bugs.root_cause: topk_softmax_with_capacity selected topk first then applied softmax: scores=topk(logits,k=1); probs=softmax(scores,dim=-1). With k=1, softmax of a length-1 vector is constant 1.0 with zero gradient w.r.t. logits, so the router weight received no learning signal at all when topk=1.
bugs.invariant: When moe_router_topk==1, the gradient of router probs w.r.t. router logits at the selected expert must be non-zero in expectation.

bugs.title: ChainedOptimizer.load_state_dict leaves param_groups stale after EP>1 checkpoint resume
bugs.root_cause: ChainedOptimizer.load_state_dict iterated over inner optimizers and called their load_state_dict, but never rebuilt self.param_groups. Inner optimizers' load_state_dict replaces their internal param_groups dict, so the outer ChainedOptimizer kept references to the OLD param_groups. Subsequent learning-rate updates went to a detached groups list and never reached the actual optimizer state, silentl
bugs.invariant: After ChainedOptimizer.load_state_dict, self.param_groups must be the concatenation of optimizer.param_groups for each inner optimizer (identity match).

bugs.title: MoE local_indices wrong via fancy indexing on bool mask when topk > 1
bugs.root_cause: BaseMoELayer used local_indices = global_indices[global_local_map] (fancy indexing). For 2-D global_indices with topk>1, advanced indexing collapses dimensions in a way that breaks the (token, expert_slot) layout, resulting in tokens being routed to the wrong experts on each EP rank. masked_select preserves the correct flat ordering.
bugs.invariant: local_indices.shape must equal global_local_map.sum() and the values must be the masked-selected entries of global_indices in row-major order.

bugs.title: MTP per-layer loss overwritten instead of accumulated when log_interval > 1
bugs.root_cause: MTPLossLoggingHelper.save_loss_to_tracker assigned total_loss_dict[name] = loss for each iteration regardless of whether the key already existed. Across multiple training iterations within one logging window, only the most recent iteration's MTP loss survived; the logged value was the last-step loss rather than the average over log_interval steps.
bugs.invariant: Within a single log_interval window, total_loss_dict[mtp_name] must equal the running sum of mtp_losses[i] across iterations until the window flushes.

bugs.title: MXFP8 reuse_grad_buf pollutes main grads on first iter when forward_pre_hook is disabled
bugs.root_cause: train_step unconditionally called optim_instance._copy_main_params_to_param_buffer() whenever reuse_grad_buf_for_mxfp8_param_ag and overlap_param_gather were both set. On the first iteration the forward_pre_hook is disabled, so finish_param_sync() never zeros the grad buffer; copying main params into the shared param/grad buffer therefore left main param values inside main_grad, silently turning t
bugs.invariant: Before the first backward of any iteration, every weight's main_grad should be all zeros (or the residual of unfinished accumulation), never equal to the param data.

bugs.title: MLA softmax_scale built from wrong mscale config field
bugs.root_cause: MultiLatentAttention computed softmax_scale as _yarn_get_mscale(rotary_scaling_factor, self.config.mscale) instead of self.config.mscale_all_dim. DeepSeek-V2 uses different values for the two; using mscale alone produced an attention softmax scaling that was wrong by an mscale_all_dim/mscale ratio, silently distorting attention probabilities every step.
bugs.invariant: MultiLatentAttention.softmax_scale must equal mscale*mscale/sqrt(q_head_dim) where mscale = _yarn_get_mscale(rotary_scaling_factor, config.mscale_all_dim).

bugs.title: cross_entropy backward inplace corruption on fp32 logits
bugs.root_cause: VocabParallelCrossEntropy.calculate_logits_max calls .float() on fp32 input which returns the same tensor; subsequent in-place subtraction corrupts activations saved for autograd backward
bugs.invariant: After .float() conversion, the result must not alias the original tensor when in-place operations follow

bugs.title: ViT local layer spec uses AttnMaskType.causal instead of no_mask, silently turning bidirectional self-attention into cau
bugs.root_cause: get_vit_layer_with_local_spec set self_attention attn_mask_type to AttnMaskType.causal. ViTs require bidirectional attention over patch tokens, so a lower-triangular mask is applied by DotProductAttention every forward pass. The TE path was already correct (no_mask) by an earlier fix; only the local path was missed. Training proceeds normally, but every patch can only attend to earlier patches, di
bugs.invariant: ViT SelfAttention.attn_mask_type must be AttnMaskType.no_mask in both TE and local layer specs.

bugs.title: prepare_input_tensors_for_wgrad_compute does not enforce all_gathered_input.contiguous(), so wgrad GEMM reads a non-cont
bugs.root_cause: prepare_input_tensors_for_wgrad_compute only called grad_output.contiguous() and assumed all_gathered_input was already contiguous. Some upstream paths (NeMo SFT QAT inputs, some reshape/transpose chains) hand in a strided tensor, but fused_weight_gradient_mlp_cuda.wgrad_gemm_accum_* indexes the buffer via flat data_ptr arithmetic. The kernel reads the wrong elements yet the tensor metadata looks
bugs.invariant: all_gathered_input.is_contiguous() must be True at the entry of prepare_input_tensors_for_wgrad_compute.

bugs.title: tensor_parallel.checkpoint runs CheckpointFunction during CUDA graph warmup, causing graph capture to record stale recom
bugs.root_cause: tensor_parallel.checkpoint always dispatched to CheckpointFunction.apply, even during graph warmup or capture. CheckpointFunction tries to recompute the saved forward inside the graph context, which corrupts the captured graph because random states and saved tensors get rewritten between warmup and capture passes. The result is a captured graph that on replay produces values that do not match the
bugs.invariant: When is_graph_warmup() or is_graph_capturing() is True, tensor_parallel.checkpoint must invoke function(*args) directly without entering CheckpointFunction.apply.

bugs.title: _CudagraphReplayNode unconditionally copies user_input into cudagraph_input even when the data pointers already match, o
bugs.root_cause: When the user_input tensor is the SAME storage as cudagraph_input (data_ptr equality), copy_ amounts to a self-copy that semantically still launches a kernel. In specific reuse patterns the source and destination data pointers were intentionally identical so no copy was needed, but cudagraph_input.copy_(user_input) was always issued and could overwrite a value that another op had just written, esp
bugs.invariant: cudagraph_input.copy_(user_input) must only be issued when user_input.data_ptr() != cudagraph_input.data_ptr().

bugs.title: DDP cast cudagraph manager runs warmup steps and shares mempool across virtual pipeline stages, corrupting captured para
bugs.root_cause: _ParamAndGradBucketGroup created a CudaGraphManager for copy_params_from_grad_buffer without num_warmup_steps=0, so the cast graph was warmed up before capture. Combined with cuda_graph_use_single_mempool=True and lack of per-VPP stage scoping, multiple VPP stages shared mempool and warmup buffers, so the captured cast graph for one VPP stage could write into another stage's parameter buffer.
bugs.invariant: DDP cast cudagraphs must be created with num_warmup_steps=0 and tagged with the current vp_stage so that VPP stages do not share captured buffer pools.

bugs.title: DistributedOptimizer FP32 shard_model_param uses non-detached view, so the parameter shard participates in autograd and
bugs.root_cause: _build_model_and_main_param_groups built shard_model_param as model_param.view(-1)[range] without .detach(). Unlike the FP16/BF16 branch (which goes through main_param.detach() copies), the FP32 view kept grad_fn alive. As soon as anything autograd-eligible touched the shard, an extra grad chain was created, leading to silently doubled gradient contributions for FP32 parameters and inconsistent st
bugs.invariant: Every shard_model_param entry created in _build_model_and_main_param_groups must satisfy shard_model_param.requires_grad == False and shard_model_param.grad_fn is None.

bugs.title: _ParamAndGradBucket builds local param_to_index from naive concatenation, ignoring per-param padding so optimizer reads
bugs.root_cause: _ParamAndGradBucket initialized param_to_index by walking params and assigning offset += param.numel(), but the global param_index_map already had per-param padded offsets. The two layouts diverged whenever a param's size was not a multiple of dp_world_size. param_to_index was then used by the distributed optimizer to slice param_data, so the optimizer wrote/read different slices than where the gr
bugs.invariant: For every param in bucket, bucket.param_to_index[param] must equal (param_index_map[param][0] - bucket.offset, param_index_map[param][1] - bucket.offset).

bugs.title: _CudagraphReplayNode treats fp4_enabled as fp8 only, skipping the per-module FP-recipe restoration on FP4 paths so saved
bugs.root_cause: _CudagraphReplayNode.forward only checked runner.fp8_enabled when deciding whether to set is_first_microbatch and restore the per-module DelayedScaling recipe. With FP4 active but FP8 inactive, the recipe restore branch was skipped, so each replay used a stale amax history. Every step shifted the FP4 scale away from the target, causing slowly drifting numerics.
bugs.invariant: If runner.fp4_enabled, the per-module DelayedScaling recipe restoration must execute identically to the runner.fp8_enabled path.

bugs.title: _CudaGraphRunner enables FP8 capture for keep-mamba-stack-attention-linear-in-bf16 layers, casting frozen-bf16 attention
bugs.root_cause: _CudaGraphRunner.__init__ set self.fp8_enabled = config.fp8 is not None / self.fp4_enabled = config.fp4 is not None unconditionally. The mamba-stack attention linears, however, are kept in bf16 to preserve numerics. Capturing those layers with FP8 enabled wrapped their GEMMs in FP8 cast paths, silently quantizing weights that were intentionally meant to stay in bf16.
bugs.invariant: If isinstance(base_module, TransformerLayer) and config.keep_mamba_stack_attention_linear_in_bf16 and not is_moe_layer, runner.fp8_enabled and runner.fp4_enabled must both be False.

bugs.title: TransformerLayer with moe_layer_recompute uses non-FP4-aware te_checkpoint guard, so FP4 recompute uses tensor_parallel.
bugs.root_cause: TransformerLayer.forward selected te_checkpoint only when self.config.fp8. With FP4-only training, the gate was False, so the regular tensor_parallel.checkpoint was used. That recompute path does not know about TE's FP recipe machinery: amax history is not extended for the recomputed forward, so the next forward sees an amax that omits the contribution of the recomputed pass, yielding mismatched s
bugs.invariant: When self.is_moe_layer and self.moe_layer_recompute and (config.fp8 or config.fp4), te_checkpoint must be selected as the recompute function.

bugs.title: group_limited_topk uses num_groups instead of topk in inner topk
Attention.set_save_original_input gate is FP8-only and missed for NVFP4, so attention activations are cached as the FP4-
bugs.root_cause: Attention.__init__ guarded set_save_original_input on the linear_proj only when config.fp8 and recipe != delayed. With FP4 training, the guard never fired so linear_proj kept the FP4-quantized tensor cache. When selective recompute later invoked the saved tensor for backward, it operated on the quantized tensor instead of the bf16 original input, producing a recompute that mismatches the forward.
bugs.invariant: set_save_original_input must be called on TELinear modules whenever (config.fp8 with non-delayed recipe and TE>=2.6.0dev0) OR (config.fp4 and TE>=2.7.0.dev0).

bugs.title: MultimodalRotaryEmbedding slices rotary embedding along the wrong dimension and omits cp_group when CP is enabled, so ea
bugs.root_cause: After emb.transpose(0, 1).contiguous() the sequence dimension is index 0, but get_pos_emb_on_this_cp_rank was called with seq_dim=1 and no cp_group argument. The wrong axis was sharded across CP ranks, and the default global cp_group fallback was used instead of the configured one. Each CP rank ended up with a rotary slice that does not correspond to its own sequence partition.
bugs.invariant: MultimodalRotaryEmbedding output for CP rank r must equal get_pos_emb_on_this_cp_rank(global_emb, seq_dim=0, group=cp_group) for the configured cp_group.

bugs.title: MambaStack assigns make_viewless_tensor result to local 'output' but returns 'hidden_states', sending a non-viewless ali
bugs.root_cause: MambaStack.forward stored the result of make_viewless_tensor in a local variable 'output', but the function ultimately returned hidden_states. So the explicit make_viewless_tensor call had no effect. The non-viewless tensor (still a view onto an internal buffer) was returned and forwarded to the next PP stage via isend; on a hybrid VPP schedule the underlying buffer was reused before isend complet
bugs.invariant: MambaStack.forward must return a tensor that is viewless (.is_view() == False) so its storage is not aliased with internal stack buffers.

bugs.title: Hybrid DSL CommonLayerConfig does not derive params_dtype from mixed_precision_dtype, so models with mixed_precision_dty
bugs.root_cause: The DSL allowed bf16 mixed-precision compute while keeping params_dtype at fp32, producing a TransformerConfig with bf16=True but params_dtype=torch.float32. The legacy --bf16 CLI path automatically aligns params_dtype with bf16, so the DSL path silently diverged: parameters were materialized in fp32 and then cast on every forward, doubling memory and changing numerics relative to the legacy path.
bugs.invariant: When TransformerConfig.bf16 is True (mixed_precision_dtype='bf16') and the recipe leaves params_dtype at the fp32 default, the produced TransformerConfig.params_dtype must equal torch.bfloat16.

bugs.title: MegatronOptimizer.get_grads_for_norm checks fsdp_param BEFORE precision-aware-optimizer branch, so M-FSDP + precision-aw
bugs.root_cause: MegatronOptimizer.get_grads_for_norm gated on getattr(param, '__fsdp_param__', False) FIRST and only fell back to the precision-aware decoupled_grad branch when not an FSDP param. With both flags on, FSDP parameters were always read via param.grad._local_tensor instead of param.decoupled_grad. Under precision-aware optimizer, param.grad is None or stale because gradients are written into param.dec
bugs.invariant: When config.use_precision_aware_optimizer_no_fp8_or_ds_fp8 is True, get_grads_for_norm must use param.decoupled_grad (with ._local_tensor when also __fsdp_param__) and never use param.grad.

bugs.title: Hybrid MoE pad_granularity is set to 32 (MXFP8) instead of 128 (HybridEP), so per-CP-rank sequence shards are misaligned
bugs.root_cause: HybridCPDataLoaderWrapper used pad_granularity = 32 (MXFP8 block size) when computing per-rank padding. HybridEP requires alignment to 128 elements. With granularity 32, per-CP-rank shards landed at offsets that did not satisfy HybridEP's 128-element alignment, so the dispatcher's load/store kernels read/wrote across token boundaries, mixing tokens between adjacent ranks.
bugs.invariant: HybridCPDataLoaderWrapper.pad_granularity must equal 128 when HybridEP is enabled (instead of 32).

bugs.title: MegatronOptimizer uses use_precision_aware_optimizer instead of use_precision_aware_optimizer_no_fp8_or_ds_fp8 when sele
bugs.root_cause: MegatronOptimizer.get_grads_for_norm and clip_grad_by_total_norm_fp32 dispatched on self.config.use_precision_aware_optimizer. With FP8 enabled, decoupled_grad is intentionally NOT used for those parameters; they should fall back to param.grad. The buggy gate took the precision-aware path anyway, attempting to read param.decoupled_grad (which is None), so grads_for_norm came back empty and grad_no
bugs.invariant: When config.fp8 is set or config.fp8_recipe in the DS_FP8 family, get_grads_for_norm must follow the param.grad branch (not param.decoupled_grad).

bugs.title: config.softmax_scale ignored in attention forward paths
RMSNorm uses L2 norm instead of root-mean-square — wrong normalization
bugs.root_cause: x.norm(2) is L2 norm (sqrt(sum(x^2))), not RMS (sqrt(mean(x^2)))
bugs.invariant: After RMSNorm, output.pow(2).mean(-1) should be approximately 1.0

bugs.title: FLOPs counter multiplies per-sequence flops by global batch size every step instead of accumulating per token
bugs.root_cause: num_fwd_flops/num_bck_flops were computed per sequence (multiplied by max_sequence_length) and SpeedMonitor accumulated them with global_batch_size every step using +=. After resume, the running total was overwritten/reset per step rather than treated as cumulative tokens, so reported Gflops did not accumulate across resumes. Fix changes flops to per-token and assigns Gflops = (fwd+bck) * global_t
bugs.invariant: total_training_Gflops must be a strictly non-decreasing function of global_total_tokens across training resumes

bugs.title: torch.device('mps') used as boolean check is always truthy, forces every run into MPS/CPU mode
bugs.root_cause: The condition `if torch.device('mps')` is always True because torch.device(...) returns a non-None Device object. As a result the script unconditionally rewrites init_device to 'mps' and disables distributed training even on CUDA hosts. Fix replaces the call with torch.backends.mps.is_available() and a corresponding CPU check.
bugs.invariant: after script bootstrap, cfg.distributed_strategy and cfg.model.init_device must reflect the actual available backend (CUDA when torch.cuda.is_available())
